cues.text: Come in!
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Professor Dundee? We’re ready to make our presentation.
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: Oh, yes. I did say one o’clock, didn’t I? Please, sit down. So, who goes first? Bruce? Or you, Betty?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: I guess I could. Bruce is always a little shy.
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: Not after he’s had a lager for lunch, eh Bruce?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Heh, heh. No, Betty really should go first.
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: OK. Well, I’m reporting on the eﬀects of diﬀerent marketing strategies on  the cheese and oil markets. Diﬀerent strategies obviously aﬀect the sales volume differently. I looked at the sales in two countries, New Zealand and Colombia.
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: And what did you find, pray tell?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, in New Zealand, the sales of both oil and cheese have declined pretty steadily. And in fact, the sales have decreased more quickly than the population. On the other hand, in Colombia, the volume of sales of both products has remained the same.
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: Wait, so you said sales in New Zealand have been going down?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Correct. Suppliers have introduced two new upscale brands of each product, which are a bit expensive but very tasty. The big ad agencies are trying out a new series of ads that shift the focus from health to great taste. They think that will get sales moving up in New Zealand, where the population is less aﬄuent and generally less health-conscious.
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: Brilliant. Thank you. And Bruce?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Uhhh... yeah. My report is about chocolate sales in Italy and Germany. The two countries’ marketers have found out that you have to market chocolate differently in each country.
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: For example?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: In Italy, “Kostig”, the most expensive brand, pays shop owners to put the candy just about knee-high for an adult.
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: I don't see...
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: For little kids, that’s about eye level! That bright red candy is the ﬁrst one they see, so they buy it! Even better, they start telling their moms to buy it, too!
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: So, you mean...
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, I mean, in Italy if you locate your product at the right location of shelves, sales do great. They say it doesn’t matter much what brand of chocolate you’re selling. As for Germany...
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: “Das Land der Schokolade”.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Huh?
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: That’s German. It means “The Land of Chocolate”. Germans love the stuff, so people make a joke and call Germany that.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Oh... uh, right...
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: So, you were saying?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: Well, like you pointed out, Germans love chocolate. But they’re thrifty. For a long time, the biggest selling brand was “Schmutzig", mostly because it was the second cheapest but didn't taste too bad.
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: Again brilliant! A pretty good job, both of you. Tell me, what do you plan to investigate next week?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: I’m especially interested in the eﬀects of colour on sales of products, so I’ll be looking at ads for cosmetics and cleaning products in the local market. You know, like the distinct orange colour of Mr. Muscle, lavatory cleaning products.
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: And you, Bruce?
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: I'm focusing on the eﬀects of diﬀerent containers on sales of cookies. So I’m going to look into packaging for cookies and how the materials they use will aﬀect the image, and in turn sales. You know, most containers are paper, but some expensive cookies come in metal boxes. The shiny metal boxes catch people’s attention and the image remains in the memory longer.
cues.speaker: BRUCE

cues.text: Well, it sounds like you two are all set. But as always in this course, I urge you both to pay much more attention to the advertisement extensions. That’s often the key. Alright, any questions for me before you go.
cues.speaker: PROFESSOR

cues.text: No, I think I’m all set. Thanks!
cues.speaker: BETTY

cues.text: Me too. Thanks, Professor Dundee. See ya later.
cues.speaker: BRUCE
